---
title: "Python–Julia Process Protocol"
subtitle: "What crosses the process boundary for one terminal request?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design.

## Launch one process for one request

Every `solve()`, `evaluate()`, or `optimize()` request that is not already a
verified success launches one external Julia process after runtime preparation
has succeeded and an attempt has been allocated. Python passes the
canonical request file and the same-request staging directory
`attempts/.staging-<ordinal>-<uuid>/`. Julia runs with the committed project,
no user startup file, and the recorded thread count.

This boundary keeps Julia compilation, factorization reuse, root continuation,
candidate evaluation, and CMA-ES inside one process. SCNSim does not embed
libjulia through JuliaCall and does not keep a daemon whose mutable state could
outlive request identity.

Python launches an argv vector without a shell, passes the package resource
project explicitly, disables startup/history files, and fixes Julia and BLAS to
one thread. It creates a new process group so interruption cannot leave a child
backend running.

Attempt allocation is the transport boundary. It reserves the ordinal and
staging directory but does not yet publish or hash `attempt.json`. Python starts
Julia in a blocked bootstrap that may report actual thread and BLAS evidence
but cannot execute the request or emit authoritative progress/outcome until
Python supplies the finalized attempt hash.

If process creation or that bootstrap fails, Python seals one immutable
`attempt_state="allocated"` record, writes a `BackendProtocolError` failure
receipt, and promotes the attempt; the ordinal is consumed. This record contains
the prepared executable hash and Python-observed host evidence, but omits all
child-observed Julia/BLAS fields; `started_at_utc` is the allocation timestamp
in both states. If the bootstrap succeeds, Python instead
seals one immutable `attempt_state="launched"` record with those observed
fields, sends its hash to the blocked child, and only then authorizes request
execution. The in-memory bootstrap framing is internal process control, not a
second request authority or durable artifact. No Julia `outcome.json` exists on
the allocated-failure path.

## Use files for authority and JSONL for progress

The request file is the only command authority. A stdout line is progress only
when it validates as `schema="scnsim.progress"`, `schema_version=1`, binds the
exact request/attempt hashes, and declares one completed optimization
generation plus evaluation-budget counts. Every other stdout line and all
stderr are logs. Python may consume valid progress for internal presentation or
diagnostics, but V1 exposes no public progress toggle or callback. Malformed
progress cannot alter the request or final outcome.

Julia writes the schema-validated `outcome.json` envelope and referenced
artifacts into staging. The envelope binds request, attempt, semantic runtime,
terminal status, typed result or failure, and the exact artifact inventory. It
does not write the final SCNSim receipt. Python waits for process completion,
validates schemas, relative paths, hashes, dimensions, and expected artifact
inventory, then seals the receipt last, fsyncs, and atomically promotes the
sibling staging directory. A promoted valid outcome keeps the authoritative
name `outcome.json`, and its SHA-256 is linked by the receipt. Invalid raw
outcome bytes may be retained only under `logs/`, never under that name.

A completed Julia success or Julia typed-failure attempt requires both process
exit status zero and one valid matching outcome. Exit zero without that
envelope, or any nonzero exit even if staging resembles an outcome, is
`BackendProtocolError`. A pre-launch failure uses the Python-sealed protocol
failure path above instead of inventing an exit status or outcome envelope.

## Make interruption an attempt outcome

On `KeyboardInterrupt`, Python terminates the child process group, waits five
seconds, kills the group if needed, validates whatever staging evidence
remains, records an interrupted attempt, and re-raises the interrupt. A later
identical operation creates a new attempt. No public timeout, cancel handle, or
JobRef is added.

An interrupted receipt does not require Julia to have reached `outcome.json`.
If an outcome exists it is validated, but no staged Result is promoted after
the interrupt. A crash-left hidden staging directory is not an attempt and is
cleaned by the next exclusive writer.

Outside that explicit interrupt path, protocol failure, invalid JSON, an
unexpected file, missing outcome, or
runtime-identity mismatch fails the whole attempt. Every declared artifact path
must be normalized, relative, contain no `..`, traverse no symlink, and resolve
inside the attempt-staging root. An absolute or escaping path is rejected
before any artifact is opened. A numerical failure that the operation contract
can represent remains typed numerical evidence instead of becoming a transport
error.
